title: Classify risk before choosing the process lane
summary: Do not choose review weight by habit. Classify reversibility, authority, externality, and protected effects first; the implementing agent owns that classification instead of pushing process routing to the human.
ai_value: Helps agents keep low-risk work fast without letting high-risk, external, or authority-changing work bypass independent review and gates.

contexts: an AI-managed codebase or knowledge base has both low-risk owner-local work and high-risk shared or protected work
the agent is deciding whether to use direct local checks, independent review, formal PR, or protected gate workflow
process overhead is either slowing safe work or being skipped for risky work

trigger_signals.description: The agent is applying the same heavy review path to every small local change.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Classify whether the work actually needs the strict lane.

trigger_signals.description: The agent wants to skip review because the change feels small but it touches authority, publication, security, data, billing, or external contributors.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Classify protected effects before choosing the fast lane.

negative_signals.description: The process lane is mandated by a maintainer, regulation, contract, or repository rule.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Follow the mandate; classification can explain but not override it.

negative_signals.description: The human is making a true business tradeoff, not choosing mechanics.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Escalate the business decision; keep technical routing with the agent after the decision.

common_wrong_assumptions: Strict review is always safer no matter the cost.
The human operator should choose branch, reviewer, and CI routing for every change.

first_checks.check: Score the change on reversibility, authority, externality, and protected effects.
first_checks.why: These axes explain why the lane is fast or strict.

first_checks.check: Use the lightest lane that preserves the classified risks and required gates.
first_checks.why: This keeps process proportional instead of ceremonial.

first_checks.check: Record the classification when the lane affects merge, publication, deployment, or shared state.
first_checks.why: Future agents need to know why the process was fast or strict.

decision_rules.condition: The change is reversible, owner-local, low-risk, and has no protected effects.
decision_rules.then: Use scoped checks and direct completion evidence without adding ritual review solely for ceremony.

decision_rules.condition: The change affects authority, external participants, publication, security, live data, billing, permissions, or irreversible state.
decision_rules.then: Stop for the required gate or independent review path before durable propagation.

do_not: Do not ask the human to choose technical routing when risk classification is an agent responsibility.
Do not use “small diff” as a substitute for protected-effect analysis.
Do not impose heavy ceremony when it does not reduce the classified risk.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Classify reversibility, authority, externality, and protected effects, then choose the lightest process lane that preserves those risks.

risk.notes: This public record is de-identified. It does not authorize bypassing human, maintainer, security, publication, billing, data, or credential gates.

sources.excerpt: Two-lane review policy showed that uniform process weight either slows low-risk work or under-protects high-risk work; the non-obvious move is agent-owned risk classification before routing.
